channels.note: Param94 rotates the upper arm, Param95 foreshortens it, Param97 bends the elbow, Param98 foreshortens the forearm

palm.note: mean of ArtMesh147 vertices; a material centroid, not a joint

reach.note: direction-pair cells are 4-degree bins; a duplicated cell is a measured alternative parameter set for the same drawn configuration

proxyDrift.correction: WITHDRAWN AS A LIMITATION: the length variation recorded here is Param95 (upper) and Param98 (forearm) doing their documented perspective work, measured end to end in `perspective`. The earlier note "the native arm is a rigid chain" was wrong: the first backend pinned both channels to 0 and then reported the resulting gap as a model limitation. Proxy drift still matters for landmark accuracy, but it is not an expression limit.

precision.note: tolerances come from the measured landmark-proxy residual and bone length, not from a result that was already reviewed; foreshortening tolerance is the same 0.02 model units expressed as a length ratio

upper.note: row key is Param95; each row is [drawnUpperLengthRatio, upperHeadingDeg] over grid.param94

forearm.note: row key is Param98; each row is [drawnForearmLengthRatio, signedBendDeg] over grid.param97

perspective.correction: the earlier calibration called this variation landmark proxy drift and concluded the native arm was rigid; both claims are withdrawn

bendSurface.conclusion: a real unreachable arc remains even with both channels; crossing it must be reported as an unsupported pose change, not interpolated
bendSurface.note: bend is the signed drawn angle between the two bones, so it is a circle, not a line; the cut position is an artefact of that representation

reachable.source: measured on the actual Core with all four arm channels free

anatomicalRight.source: SecondaryArmPatch.cs constants + python mirror (verify_patch.py checks the mirror against the running Player meshes); NOT a Cubism Core measurement
anatomicalRight.projectionNote: projection scales are the only way this backend can shorten a drawn segment; upper .75..1, forearm .55..1, palm length .55..1, width .35..1
anatomicalRight.note: the patch is a mesh postprocess; it never writes Core vertices

projectionEnvelopeMeasurement.note: measured on the real triangles of the 16 target meshes across 7 joint poses; the declared C# floor for the forearm (.55) is below the measured .75, so a clip clamped only to the declared floor is rejected by the runtime preflight

corrections.claim: the native arm is a rigid chain and cannot foreshorten a segment
corrections.evidence: Param95 0..30 shrinks the drawn upper arm 0.1505 -> 0.0965 (0.64x); Param98 0..-30 shrinks the drawn forearm 0.1790 -> 0.0510 (0.285x), measured on the actual Core and visible in the mesh, not only in a landmark
corrections.cause: the first backend pinned Param95/98 to zero, so it discarded a real capability and then attributed the resulting error to the model

corrections.claim: the projected bend circle has a 12.8 degree unreachable arc
